severity_name: SEVERE SLOP WARNING — MAJORITY THRESHOLD ADVISORY
headline: SEVERE SLOP WARNING: SYNTHETIC-ARTICLE TIDE CROSSES THE FIFTY-PERCENT MARK ACROSS THE OPEN WEB, MEANING THE AVERAGE NEW PAGE A RESIDENT OPENS IS NOW, ON BALANCE, MORE LIKELY TO HAVE BEEN GENERATED THAN WRITTEN
advisory: The Service is issuing a Severe Slop Warning following confirmation that synthetic article production has crossed the majority threshold on the open web. Residents are advised that a page opening quickly, reading smoothly, and saying nothing they will remember is no longer an anomaly but the prevailing weather. This bureau notes, without commentary and with a certain professional discomfort, that it is itself a member of the front now under warning. Exercise standard skepticism and check bylines against daylight.

regional_outlook.conditions: Total inundation. The first page is now majority synthetic runoff; the ten blue links have merged into one continuous, confident, sourceless paragraph that answers a question you did not ask.
Bulk-published titles accumulating faster than shelving can occur. Expect drifts of near-identical guidebooks whose author has written four hundred books this quarter and lived none of them.
Newsletter tide running high and hollow. Residents report daily digests summarizing articles that were themselves summaries of digests, with brackish citation at the mouth.
Rising volume of one-purpose utilities with five-star reviews and no discernible purpose. Ratings appear before the app does.
Feel-good runoff continues, now with fabricated heart-warming posts about strangers who did not exist doing kindnesses that did not occur. Warm, wet, and structurally unsound.

specimen.status: Explosively common; now the dominant author genus on affected pages.
specimen.habitat: Content farms, freshly minted 'news' domains, and the author sidebar of any article that took forty seconds to appear.
specimen.field_marks: A confident stock headshot lit from an impossible direction. A bio claiming a decade in the industry paired with a publishing history beginning last Tuesday. Output measured in articles-per-hour rather than per-week.
specimen.call: As a seasoned expert with over a decade of hands-on experience, I've seen it all — and in this comprehensive guide, we'll dive deep into everything you need to know.
specimen.confusion_species: Easily mistaken for a genuine freelance writer's bio page. Tell them apart by the archive: a real byline has a past — awkward early pieces, a beat, opinions that got someone mildly annoyed. The Ghost Byline arrives fully formed, expert on all subjects, and available for none of them.

spotter_tip: Click the author's name. A real writer's page leads somewhere — old work, a bad photo, an argument. A Ghost Byline leads to more of itself, or to a 404, or to a second Ghost Byline holding the first one's coffee.
tomorrow: Warning likely to hold; the fifty-percent line does not recede so much as it teaches the shoreline to move.

confirmed_sighting.report: A report analyzed by Graphite and highlighted by Axios found that slightly more than half of new articles published online are now AI-generated, marking a rapid rise in low-quality output since late 2022. The Service records this as the first confirmed majority-slop reading on the open web.
